topics.name: Anwen
topics.title: Oren's coat
topics.summary: Ask about the coat Oren left behind.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You still have Oren's coat.

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: The cuff is stiff with mud. I keep folding that part underneath.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What happens if you wash it?

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: Then it's a clean coat. I know that, but I keep behaving as if I'll have sent him away a second time.

topics.name: Anwen
topics.title: The basket handles
topics.summary: Talk about the baskets returned from the household deliveries.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You kept the empty baskets?

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: For the next meals. One handle's nearly through, and the woman who carried it apologized to me.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: For the handle?

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: For needing the basket. I started explaining why she needn't, then I fetched some twine.

topics.name: Mira
topics.title: The labels in your hand
topics.summary: Ask about the labels on Mira's medicines.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You've rewritten the labels.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The first ones were tidy and small. Especially the word ash.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Too small to read?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: No, small enough for me to hope they wouldn't. These are less tidy.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: New labels?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: For the clean roots. I found room to write every steeping time.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: And the other jar?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Still the old label. I keep finding very necessary work on the other side of the table.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You reached for that empty space.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The old jar stood there for years. My hand gets ahead of me.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What brings it back?

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The kettle; the clean roots need longer, so I watch them. Waiting turns out to be part of treating someone.

topics.name: Rook
topics.title: What Bram charged
topics.summary: Remember the man who used to repair Rook's cart.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Bram charged you for only one axle.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The second repair was free if I held the wheel and stopped advising him.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Did you manage both?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The wheel stayed up. He took what victories he could.

topics.name: Rook
topics.title: Can I still ask about the road?
topics.summary: Ask what Rook is comfortable discussing now.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Can I still ask about the road?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: You can ask. If I say a place stays off the page, it stays off.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Even when the route passes it?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Especially then. A road goes past a great many doors it hasn't been invited through.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Can I still ask about the road?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Here, where I can see who's coming.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You used to answer with a joke.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: I still have them. I'm saving the good ones for a room that doesn't feel like an address you've handed out.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Can I still ask about the road?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Ask where it goes. Don't ask me to draw the houses back in.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You remember them all?

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: The doors, mostly, and which ones opened. A blank sheet doesn't make that a blank part of my life.

topics.name: Tor
topics.title: The grinding stone
topics.summary: Ask about the tool Tor used on the old iron.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What did you use to grind the marks away?

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: That stone. Still cuts.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Why keep it beside the named work?

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: So I have to reach past it. I said 'still useful' about the iron, too, and I don't want the words coming out before I've thought.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What did you use to grind the marks away?

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: That stone. Still cuts.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You still use it?

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: On an edge, not on a name. I can remember the difference without pretending I need a different stone.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What did you use to grind the marks away?

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: That stone. It wasn't in the bundle I handed over.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Forgotten?

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: No, the families decide what happens to their iron. This bit is mine to remember.

topics.name: Tor
topics.title: How I held the hammer
topics.summary: Ask what Tor noticed during the road repair.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What was wrong with my grip?

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: You held the hammer as if the board might answer back.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I've worked with worse company.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: Board's better company if you loosen your thumb. Head does the striking.

topics.name: Edric
topics.title: The seal in your hand
topics.summary: Ask Edric about a familiar habit now that the renewal has stopped.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You keep turning the seal in your hand.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I used to do that while someone gave me a number. It made an answer wait until I was ready for it.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Does it help now?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: No, I'm discovering how long a silence can be when nobody has to fill it for me.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You still have the seal.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: You have the ledger. Must I empty my pockets for this conversation?

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I asked about the seal.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: It used to mean people waited for my answer. Now they watch for what I'll try to keep.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You've rubbed the edge of the seal smooth.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: It was smooth before you arrived.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I didn't notice.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: You were occupied with getting an answer out of me. This one, at least, I can give without your help.

topics.name: Senn
topics.title: Reading their refusal
topics.summary: Ask Senn what he heard in the deserters' written refusal.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You read their refusal?

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: Twice. First I looked for a sentence someone must have put in their mouths.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: And the second?

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: I recognized the way they complain. I used to interrupt before they reached the point.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You read their refusal?

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: The copy with the homes left out. I noticed the gaps before I listened to the words.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Did the gaps change what they said?

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: No, they just left me fewer places to look instead.

topics.name: Halvern
topics.title: Let the words rest
topics.summary: Stay a moment with the preserved sanctuary memory.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: The sanctuary order is copied. You don't have to give it again.

lines.speaker: Halvern
lines.text: Sanctuary under the Vargan seal.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I have that line.

lines.speaker: Halvern
lines.text: Do not close it. There are still people on the road.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I hear you.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What do you do when nobody needs you?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: I usually discover that the linen needs me. It is very persuasive linen.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: And if I hid the basket?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: I'd sit outside. There is a patch of afternoon sun beside the wall.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you want company?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: For five minutes. You may tell me something that doesn't require an answer.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Does anyone ever refuse your help?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: Nessa has forbidden me to season the stew. She was quite firm.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: How bad was it?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: People were very thirsty. I thought that was encouraging at first.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Have you tried again?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Anwen
lines.text: I chop onions now. Nessa tastes it, and I try to leave the spoon alone.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you always explain why you lost?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Only when the explanation is more interesting than the game.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: And when it isn't?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Then I improve it. The light is usually at fault.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You could just say I played well.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: You played well. There. An exhausting afternoon's honesty. Shall we have another?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you ever run out of things to say?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Frequently. I keep three old stories ready so nobody notices.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I notice the one about the shortcut.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Everyone notices that one. It's still quicker than admitting I'm tired.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You can be tired here.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Rook
lines.text: Good. Sit where you can watch the door. I would like to stop doing it for a little while.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Are all the flowers you keep useful?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: The yellow ones are dreadful medicine. Very cheerful, though.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You planted them for the color?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Yes. Toma calls them weeds with ambition. I like them better for it.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Will they stay?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: As long as they leave room for the roots I need. I can want two things in one garden.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

topics.name: Mira
topics.title: What you read in the rain
topics.summary: What you read in the rain.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What do you read when the weather keeps you indoors?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Travel accounts. Especially the ones written by people who plainly got lost.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: For the descriptions?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: For the corrections. You can hear them getting less certain as the pages go on.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Would you make the journeys yourself?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: One or two. Somewhere with a warm room at the end, preferably. I'm quite adventurous about warm rooms.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Have you ever made something just because you liked its shape?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: A little iron bird. Very poor at being a hook.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Was it meant to be a hook?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: That is what I told people. It was meant to be a bird.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you still have it?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: Somewhere safe. I might try another. The wings were better than the feet.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Are you a patient teacher?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: Until somebody picks up the tool. Then my hands start reaching for it.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: That sounds familiar.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: I know exactly where their thumb should go. Saying it is harder than moving it.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: How do you stop yourself?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Tor
lines.text: Hands behind my back. If you see me standing like an officer, somebody is learning something.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What would you change about your room?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Elna
lines.text: Something blue. I haven't decided what. Everyone asks what size I need before asking what I like.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What sort of blue?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Elna
lines.text: Dark enough to look green when the light goes. I saw it once on a traveler's sleeve.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You remembered the sleeve.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Elna
lines.text: I remembered wanting it. That surprised me more.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

topics.name: Elna
topics.title: How to be a good visitor
topics.summary: How to be a good visitor.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What makes a good visitor?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Elna
lines.text: One who moves the basket before sitting down. You are improving.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Anything else?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Elna
lines.text: Ask an ordinary question sometimes. What I ate. Whether the roof kept the rain out.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What did you eat?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Elna
lines.text: Bread with too much butter. I enjoyed every bit. You may look less worried now.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Does your daughter take your advice?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: She listens closely, which fooled me for quite a while.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Then does what she intended?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: Sometimes she tries it my way first. I almost find that worse when hers works better.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you tell her?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: Eventually. She has learned to wait with a very patient expression. I wonder where she got it.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: How do you know when the day's work is finished?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: I don't. Usually somebody starts supper without me.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Does the work suffer if you stop?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: Most of it waits perfectly well. I come back and find it exactly as annoying as before.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Then why stay?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Toma
lines.text: I like going indoors with an answer ready. Sometimes I ought to go indoors with muddy boots and no answer.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You nearly gave that as an order.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: I heard it too. The first word came out before I had chosen the rest.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What were you trying to ask?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: Whether there was room for me at the bench. I made it sound like an inspection.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You could try the question again.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: Would there be room? You needn't answer quickly. I am trying to remember that part.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You were tapping out a tune.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: An old marching song. I cannot remember the second verse.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Did you ever know it?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: Probably not. We all sang the first verse louder and trusted the man beside us.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Does that bother you now?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Senn
lines.text: Sometimes. Today I would simply like to remember whether it was about rain or a missing boot.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Have you ever made your own breakfast?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: That question has more accusation in it than the last three about the stores.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I was wondering about the eggs.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I can boil an egg. I have been assured that this is not a sufficient household qualification.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Who assured you?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Several people, independently. It appears to be the one matter on which the household agrees.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you play an instrument?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Badly enough that people once praised the attempt rather than the result.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Did you believe them?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: At first. Then somebody who had not seen me laughed outside the door.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Did you keep playing?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: In private. I would rather have learned to hear the wrong note sooner.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you write anything for yourself?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Vale
lines.text: Descriptions of weather, lately. They are all much too long.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Let me hear one.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Vale
lines.text: No. I would begin correcting it as soon as you listened, and it would become work.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Then I won't ask again.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Vale
lines.text: You may ask whether I wrote today. That is a different question.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You have ink on your sleeve.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Vale
lines.text: Yes. I was drawing something in the margin and leaned across it.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What were you drawing?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Vale
lines.text: A bird. It has too many feet. I kept starting the feet again.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Will you scrape it off?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Vale
lines.text: I think I'll keep it. It is unmistakably mine.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Does your tea always go cold?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Merrow
lines.text: It is usually the first thing I prepare and the last thing I remember.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I can wait while you drink it.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Merrow
lines.text: That is unexpectedly difficult to accept. I keep wanting to find you something to read.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: I am comfortable waiting.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Merrow
lines.text: Then I shall try being comfortable drinking. A moment, please.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you take the shortest way home?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Merrow
lines.text: Through the service passage. Except when I take the garden gate, which adds seven minutes.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: You have timed it?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Merrow
lines.text: Once. Then several more times to make sure I wasn't hurrying.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What is worth the seven minutes?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Merrow
lines.text: The sound changes outside the walls. I like arriving home after I have stopped hearing the office.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What do you make when you aren't baking?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nessa
lines.text: Small animals from scrap wood. Rook says they are all potatoes with ears.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Is he right?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nessa
lines.text: About the horse. The badger is very good. I refuse to hear otherwise.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Who gets them?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nessa
lines.text: Whoever asks nicely. I keep the badger. An artist is allowed one satisfied customer.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you ever eat at someone else's table?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nessa
lines.text: I try. Then I see how they have stacked the bowls and start rearranging them.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What if they ask you to sit down?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nessa
lines.text: I sit. I notice the bowls from there as well.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Perhaps they want your company.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nessa
lines.text: That is what Elna said. Quite sharply, in fact. I had a lovely evening once I believed her.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

topics.name: Nera
topics.title: A place you want to see
topics.summary: A place you want to see.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Where would you go with an empty cart?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nera
lines.text: Somewhere I had never been asked to take a cart. A difficult destination to put on a map.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Sea or hills?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nera
lines.text: Hills. I would like to reach the top and have nothing to unload.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Have you chosen a route?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nera
lines.text: I'm keeping that part for myself a while. Planning it has been pleasant.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: What do your crew argue about when the road is easy?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nera
lines.text: Where to put a wet cup. It is an argument of surprising endurance.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Where do you put yours?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nera
lines.text: On top of whatever is least likely to fall. Apparently that is not a system.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Kael
lines.text: Do you settle it as their leader?
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.

lines.speaker: Nera
lines.text: They have put a small cloth beside my seat. I have decided to regard it as a treaty.
lines.direction: Quiet, conversational; let the other person finish.
